research.statement: Social supermarkets alleviate immediate food insecurity using customer-choice retail models, but remain structurally dependent on the continuous generation of commercial food surplus.
research.caveat: Synthesizes scoping literature on customer experiences and models; does not report quantitative nutritional or clinical outcomes.

research.statement: Fresh produce redistribution scenarios consistently produce net environmental benefits across five lifecycle metrics, maximized when gleaning intermediaries transport surplus directly to food pantries.
research.caveat: Parametric life cycle simulation; does not track actual nutritional uptake or consumer-level food spoilage rates.

research.statement: An IoT-enabled platform tracking temperature, humidity, and gas rescued 847 kg of surplus food and reduced pickup times by 42% in a multi-stakeholder pilot.
research.caveat: Pilot deployment outcomes reported in an abstract; does not show long-term institutional permanence, cost sustainability, or recipient nutritional impacts.

research.statement: A scoping review identified that the burden of redistributing food waste to resolve food insecurity relies heavily on under-resourced rescue charities requiring structural subsidies and nutrition expertise.
research.caveat: Scoping review of existing literature and policy recommendations; does not quantify population-level health, dietary, or nutritional impact.

research.statement: Surplus food redistribution organizations expand immediate food access but find their ability to challenge systemic causes of food precarity and waste constrained by alignments with corporate and state entities.
research.caveat: Ethnographic qualitative evaluation; does not quantify recipient nutritional security or broader poverty reduction metrics
